definition: A technique that places a sample in a strong magnetic field and records the radio waves its hydrogen nuclei absorb, showing how many different hydrogen environments a molecule has and how they are arranged.
The surroundings of a hydrogen atom in a molecule; hydrogens with identical surroundings are equivalent and give one NMR signal between them.
The position of an NMR signal, $\delta$, in parts per million (ppm) measured from the tetramethylsilane (TMS) signal at $\delta = 0$; it shows what kind of group a hydrogen is near.
A stepped line on an NMR spectrum whose step heights are in the ratio of the areas under the signals, and so of the numbers of hydrogens in each environment.
The cluster of peaks a high-resolution NMR signal splits into: $n$ non-equivalent hydrogens on the adjacent carbon atoms give $n + 1$ peaks (singlet, doublet, triplet, quartet).
